> Eyedoro is a desk buddy with two robot eyes that works as a Pomodoro study timer. Press the button to start a 25 minute work session. While you work, the eyes look around as if they are watching over you. When time is up, a beep plays and the eyes fall asleep for a 5 minute break, then a lower beep wakes them up.

## Design

### 2026-11-01: October 31 to November 1: Designed the schematic and PCB for EyesDoro (robot eyes Pomodoro timer)!

**7h**

October 31 to November 1: Designed the schematic and PCB for EyesDoro (robot eyes Pomodoro timer)!

LED matrix display for Week 4
Selecting the idea
finally it was time to make something on my own and even just deciding what i should make took load of time but I looked at the suggested projects for all seven displays and compared their duration and complexity. Many extra components were needed for NeoPixels and LED filament, and a LiPo and charging circuit were needed for OLED Pomodoro. LED matrices seemed the simple but cool option, and the Robot eyes idea sounded fun. I just added the Pomodoro part to it.

Schematic (Route A of the guide)
I selected Route A which is a pre-made MAX7219 module that plugs into a 5-pin socket. I did as per the guide's instructions, in the order they are presented:
Added Conn_01x05 as J1
Added the XIAO RP2040 symbol from the Hackclub care package. That labels the pins as GPIO numbers so I've matched up the guide's D10, D8 and D7 to GPIO3, GPIO2 and GPIO1 respectively.
Added net labels MTX_DIN, MTX_CLK and MTX_CS, plus +5V and GND
Added a 10 uF capacitor across +5V and GND
Added a button on D3 using SW_Push, one side to GND with no resistor, since the code uses INPUT_PULLUP, like in the guide’s “Adding inputs” section
Added a buzzer on D1 for the timer sounds. The guide has no buzzer wiring so that was my own pin choice.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 163015](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/1cc899e8954aca7dd5c5f7667b21343d9d753e2d0c40569f59c681d6e0bc5c26.png)

The level shifter
The guide's Route A has the XIAO straight through to the module via the steps and pin table. The Schematic checks list however states that the MAX7219 requires at least 3.5V for a logic high and the XIAO only puts out 3.3V so it says to add a level shifter. That step is in the Route B section so I wasn't sure but I went with the safety check and added a 74AHCT125 (powered from 5V), with its OE pins to GND and its own 100nF capacitor. DIN, CLK and CS all go through it.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 163056](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/7dd219bc344adf59f4f8f1142468e0dbbf3d64063b68a4d048d4c35dd4e81d36.png)

PCB
The XIAO footprint wasn't there to begin with. Fixed that by checking the Hackclub footprints library path. Drew a rect board outline of about 60 x 40mm and placed the parts. Put the level shifter between the XIAO and J1 to keep the signals as short as possible and the caps right up against their chips.

![Screenshot 2026-11-01 163618](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/gfWl2tMDbbFllUPCOWxRpQb4XDb3SDLx/46345e5b8966b0b0c88db53e0aba5823cb6721b53035ef003a07d84b02d994d8.png)
I followed the guide’s routing notes:

Running DRC
DRC came back with 0 violations but one unconnected item: pad 10 (GND) on the level shifter wasn't connected to its via. I connected that up, refilled the zone and ran DRC again to check. i had also mistakenly filled the zone with fcu so i change that to bcu.
